alice_support: FYI customer (acme-inc) opened an escalation — streaming response dropped mid-token and they got billed as a 5xx. request_id=r-0a1b2c4d. They sent a short trace and curl output.

alice_support: Repro summary they gave: single streaming completion, last chunk arrives partially, then client sees ECONNRESET while our gateway marks it 502 and counts tokens. They insist tokens billed despite client abort. :confused:

alice_support: Attaching the snippet they used (curl):
```
curl -v -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \n  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-alpha","prompt":"x","stream":true}' \n  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream/generate\n```

alice_support: They say this happens with their internal proxy (enterprise customers often use corporate proxies). Asking if this looks like a client half-close being misclassified as gateway failure.

jason_sre: Can you paste the full gateway logs + the proxy trace id? Need to see upstream FIN/RST vs client TCP close. Our heuristics historically flagged sudden EOF as 5xx when it occurred before any outbound response bytes were flushed.

jason_sre: Also what HTTP version did their proxy use? HTTP/2 resets behave differently vs chunked HTTP/1.1.

alice_support: Proxy trace id: p-trace-9921. They reported HTTP/1.1 chunked. I've uploaded the gateway logs to the incident folder with that trace id.

maya_runtime: quick glance — log shows gateway sent a few chunk frames then saw a connection reset from client side after 1.2s of silence. Our gateway marked it as "upstream error" because it didn't see the final chunk trailer. Could be their proxy half-closing without waiting for connection drain.

maya_runtime: Two quick asks to reproduce: 1) can support run same curl with `--no-buffer` and `--http1.1`? 2) if customer can run `tcpdump -w /tmp/trace.pcap port 443 and host api.redwood.ai` during the repro, that would confirm FIN vs RST.

alice_support: I'll send the curl variants and tcpdump request. Customer asked if we can patch classification now because they're seeing unexpected charge.

suzie_support: Customer support note: they are on metered hosting tier, small monthly bill but this session produced ~1.2k billed tokens. They're asking for a refund while we investigate. I told them we'd triage ASAP and keep them posted.

jason_sre: Short-term mitigation: we can add a soft rule to not count requests as 5xx if we observed at least one token flush to client and upstream returned 200-type headers. That would avoid billing for client-abort races. Ops, is that safe?

maya_runtime: That's workable but we need to be careful: if upstream actually failed mid-render (OOM, kernel kill) and we still streamed partial tokens, we might under-count true 5xxs. Suggest a policy: if client disconnect occurs within X seconds of last token and gateway saw no upstream 500, treat as client-abort and mark non-5xx for billing. X=2s; tune after rollouts.

deploy-bot: Deployment event: net-proxy v1.14 deployed to prod on 2026-03-10T03:21Z (rollout 100%). No streaming heuristic changes in this release.

jason_sre: Good catch about timing window. For this specific customer, we can do one-off refund if pcap confirms client FIN. I'll take logs and coordinate with billing.

alice_support: Customer provided pcap + their proxy logs. The pcap shows client sends FIN immediately after receiving partial chunk (client timed out). Looks like a proxy-level timeout (idle timeout 30s) triggered.

maya_runtime: With that evidence I'm comfortable classifying this as client-side abort. Recommend refund and open a follow-up to add the 2s grace heuristic. I'll make a PR with tests that simulate FIN after token flush and ensure billing flag is non-5xx.

jason_sre: I'll prepare an internal postmortem to capture detection gaps and add an observability metric: fraction of streaming sessions with client FIN within 0-5s after last token.

suzie_support: I'll issue the refund and send customer a summary + ETA for the heuristic change.

alice_support: Thanks all. Action items:
- alice_support: collect final artifacts and confirm refund done (assigned to me).
- jason_sre: postmortem + billing coordination.
- maya_runtime: PR for 2s grace heuristic + unit tests.
- suzie_support: customer comms.

alice_support: tagging @jason_sre @maya_runtime for visibility. :thumbsup:

jason_sre: +1. Keeping this channel for updates, will DM billing for the refund confirmation.
